Solution: A mobile-first decision-support app that ranks crop rotations for a specific field and explains why each one ranks where it does.

How it works

The farmer pins a field on the map and sets priorities with sliders: save water, income, soil health and low risk.
The app pulls NASA climate and moisture signals (POWER, SMAP, MODIS NDVI, GPM IMERG), a soil estimate from SoilGrids (non-NASA), and crop requirements.
Each rotation gets scores for water, climate risk, soil benefit and income. The sliders act as weights, so the same rotations rank differently for different farmers.
The farmer sees ranked cards with stars, four indicators and a “Why?” panel, and can compare options and try what-if scenarios.

Team: [your team name and members]

One-line description
A mobile-first decision-support app that ranks crop rotations for a specific field using NASA Earth observations, a soil estimate and the farmer’s own priorities, and explains why each option ranks where it does.

Problem
Farmers face shifting temperatures, changing rainfall, water shortages and declining soil health. Old rotation habits may no longer fit, and a wrong choice costs water, money and soil quality.

Solution

  1. The farmer pins a field on the map and sets priorities with sliders: save water, income, soil health, low risk.
  2. The app pulls climate and moisture signals, a soil estimate and crop requirements.
  3. Each rotation is scored on water, climate risk, soil benefit and income. The sliders act as weights, so different farmers get different rankings from the same scores.
  4. Results appear as ranked cards with stars, four indicators and a “Why?” panel. Farmers can compare options and try what-if scenarios.

Tech stack

  • Frontend: React + Vite PWA, so it works on phones
  • Backend: FastAPI + SQLite
  • Data: mock data first, then precomputed JSON for the real NASA and soil data, with a saved fallback if an API is unavailable

Key features

  • Plot map with a SMAP moisture overlay and a time scrubber
  • Soil profile with a Low / Medium / High fertility estimate, labelled as an estimate
  • Optional Soil Health Card values that override the estimate
  • Priority sliders that re-rank rotations live
  • “Why?” explanations for each rank
  • Compare view and what-if scenarios (include these only if built)

Impact
Helps farmers explore rotations that conserve water and strengthen soil, using data that is otherwise hard for them to access. The “Why?” panel makes the advice understandable and checkable.

Limitations (stated openly)

  • Satellite and modelled data show regional trends, not field-level guarantees.
  • Soil is an estimate unless the farmer enters their own values.
  • Income is not NASA data, so it is labelled as a rough estimate.
  • The scoring rules are a prototype and not yet validated against yield data.
  • It is decision support, not a replacement for an agronomist.

Future work
More regions and crops, local soil test data, backtesting rotations against 20 years of climate, local language support, and pilots with local agriculture offices or KVKs.
